answer: Interleaved Arrival Commitment. Each identity must emit its first N messages on a fixed schedule, and any deviation resets a copper-scored reputation ledger. Agents that skip or burst their slots get throttled, so a mass-registered fleet stalls on the same queue. The cost is wall-clock time: spinning up fresh identities buys each one a slow, serialized ramp, and parallel forgery collapses into a spiral of missed deadlines. A single attacker thread cannot fake the cadence without paying real latency per account.
